summary: A well-made Pre-IELTS listening paper in true IELTS format: a booking call with spelling, corrections and changed numbers, a staff briefing with MCQ and a matching box, a two-student discussion, and a lecture with note completion. Every item has a real distractor, but the speakers signpost the answer very clearly ('What genuinely surprised us was...', 'The real problem was...'), which makes it a little gentler than a real test - right for B2 students.
strengths: Scripts are full length (612 / 668 / 889 / 709 words) and answers come in question order.
Part 1 has all the classic traps: spelling, a misheard number corrected (308562), a self-correction (160 to 165), old vs new deposit, last year's vs this year's location.
Parts 2 and 3 MCQs mention each wrong option before ruling it out; the multi-select pairs reject every distractor explicitly.
Part 4 notes follow the lecture's structure with one-word concrete answers.

issues.problem: Box option C ('will open later than the rest of the building') was word for word what the speaker says, so the item needed no paraphrase recognition.
issues.change: Box option C reworded to 'will not be ready when the rink opens'; same letter, same key.

issues.problem: Part 4 note lines for Q32, Q34, Q36 and Q37 copied the lecturer's words exactly, unlike real IELTS notes, which paraphrase.
issues.change: Note wording only (not the script): 'war divers' -> 'military divers', 'sent down from the surface' -> 'delivered from above', 'joined' -> 'attached', 'air pumped down' -> 'air supplied'. Answers unchanged.

issues.problem: 'tanks' was accepted, but the lecturer only says 'cylinders'; IELTS gap answers must be the word heard.
Paraphrase pair used 'funded by', which does not appear anywhere in the question paper.
issues.change: Pair is now ['the family firm from Winter Street', 'a local company'].

issues.problem: Paraphrase pairs for Q12 and Q14 quoted words that are not in the script.
issues.change: Q12 is now ['about lessons for themselves', 'the demand for adult lessons'] and Q14 is now ['how to avoid the wait', 'to avoid queues'].

issues.problem: Laylo says 'The poster starts conversations' almost word for word before the key, so option B is easier to match than an IELTS item would be.
issues.change: Suggestion only (the script is recorded): next time, keep the option wording out of the script.

issues.problem: Part 2 and 3 answers are strongly signposted ('What genuinely surprised us was', 'The real problem was', 'The strongest titles state'), which lowers difficulty.
issues.change: Acceptable for Pre-IELTS. For harder sets, let the correct answer come with less of a marker, or put a distractor after the answer.
